candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

Everyday I use qualities such as patience, mildness, tolerance and love in what I do.  These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor with an Ed.D. in Community Care and Counseling: Traumatology and more than 15 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, and program leadership, I bring a strong commitment to providing high-quality, trauma-informed care to adolescents and families.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with youth experiencing complex behavioral health challenges, trauma histories, family instability, and barriers to accessing appropriate treatment. In my leadership role with Partners Health Management, I have overseen behavioral health initiatives across a 15-county service area, supervised multidisciplinary teams, and helped develop and implement specialized programs designed to improve access to services, strengthen care coordination, and reduce unnecessary higher levels of care.  One of my greatest professional strengths is combining clinical expertise with operational leadership. I have experience supporting clinical decision-making, establishing effective workflows, monitoring quality and compliance, mentoring staff, and collaborating with families, community providers, hospitals, and child welfare agencies. I understand the importance of developing a clinical environment where staff feel supported, families feel heard, and adolescents receive individualized, evidence-based treatment.

My doctoral research focused on the experiences of social workers placing youth in residential treatment within North Carolina's child welfare system. This work further strengthened my understanding of the challenges adolescents and families face when appropriate community-based behavioral health services are unavailable. I am particularly passionate about developing programs that intervene earlier, promote stability, and help youth receive effective treatment in the least restrictive appropriate setting.

The opportunity to contribute to the development and leadership of Adolescent Wellness Academy's North Carolina program is especially appealing. I would welcome the opportunity to help establish a strong clinical culture, support staff development, build community partnerships, and ensure that adolescents and families receive compassionate, effective, and accountable care.  Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to adolescent mental health could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's success.

Sincerely,
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. With more than three years of experience in healthcare, care coordination, and social services, along with my ongoing Master of Social Work studies and clinical internship at Boca Recovery Center, I bring a strong foundation in patient advocacy, behavioral health support, resource navigation, and multidisciplinary collaboration.

Throughout my career, I have supported individuals and families navigating complex healthcare needs, behavioral health challenges, and difficult life transitions. My experience includes conducting assessments, developing individualized care plans, coordinating services, documenting clinical information, and helping individuals connect with resources that support their well-being. At Boca Recovery Center, I have gained additional clinical experience working with individuals affected by substance use disorders, participating in therapeutic groups, supporting recovery-oriented goals, and developing my skills in motivational interviewing and therapeutic communication.

What draws me to AWA is your commitment to looking beyond adolescents’ behaviors to understand the emotions, experiences, and challenges behind them. candidates.cover_letter:
Throughout my career, I have had the privilege of working with students from a variety of backgrounds and with a wide range of academic, behavioral, and emotional needs. My experience in special education has shaped not only the professional I am today, but also the way I view the importance of creating safe spaces for young people who may be navigating some of the most difficult seasons of their lives.

Much of my career has been dedicated to special education, and I currently work in a modified setting supporting high school students. I have also worked with middle and high school students in both Emotional or Behavioral Disabilities (EBD) and Intellectual Disabilities (IND) settings. These experiences have taught me that working with adolescents requires much more than structure and routine. It requires understanding that every young person has a story and recognizing that behavior can be a form of communication. Some of the most meaningful moments in my career have come from seeing a student make progress that others may have once thought was out of reach.

My commitment to young people extends beyond the classroom. I have worked with students throughout different parts of Miami, from South Miami to Overtown, and when I lived closer to the area, I also volunteered at the Overtown Youth Center. Those experiences helped reinforce how much a young person's environment and access to caring adults can influence their path. That belief is a major reason this opportunity resonates with me.

While my professional background is rooted in education, I have also developed valuable operational and organizational skills through my previous experience with Wix and Publix. At Publix, I gained hands-on experience helping manage front-of-house operations, coordinating with leadership, and working collaboratively on staff scheduling and coverage. I learned the importance of anticipating needs, communicating clearly, adjusting to unexpected changes, and ensuring that the people and resources around me were in the right place for the day to run successfully. Combined with my experience in education, behavioral support, documentation, and student safety, these skills have prepared me to contribute to a role that requires both compassion and strong operational judgment.

As I consider this next chapter in my career, I am looking for a path that allows me to continue making a meaningful difference while also being intentional about my future and my responsibilities to my family. My decision to explore a career transition is not a reflection of losing my passion for education or for working with young people. Rather, it comes from a desire to build on what I have learned, grow into new leadership opportunities, and continue serving adolescents and families in a different capacity. I hope to bring the perspective of an educator who understands that the people behind the daily operations matter just as much as the systems that keep a program running..

It would be an honor to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's mission and to help create an environment where adolescents feel supported and staff feel equipped to do their best work. Thank you for considering my application and for the work your organization does for young people and families throughout South Florida. I would welcome the opportunity to share more about my experience and how I hope to contribute to your team.

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., NCC
Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI)
South Florida | Hallandale Beach
Bilingual Portuguese–English Professional
561-289-5680 | paula@lm2services.com | https://www.linkedin.com/in/paula-lazarim-3a5b6127/

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern
+1 (561) 289-5680 | paula@lm2services.com

​I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. ​Joining Adolescent Wellness Academy appeals to me because of your commitment to guiding adolescents and their families toward healing and growth. ​Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background aligns with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy.
​Sincerely,
Christopher Maddocks

Although my professional background has been in healthcare finance, nonprofit leadership, and client services, my long-term career goal is to become a substance use and mental health counselor, and I am actively pursuing that transition by working toward my Credentialed Alcoholism and Substance Abuse Counselor (CASAC) certification through a New York State OASAS-approved program.

Throughout my career, I have consistently worked in environments where trust, professionalism, confidentiality, and compassionate communication were essential. Whether supporting clients as a Licensed Insurance Broker, collaborating with interdisciplinary teams within a hospital system, or serving in financial leadership roles for healthcare and nonprofit organizations, I developed skills that directly translate to behavioral health—including active listening, detailed documentation, ethical decision-making, crisis awareness, and helping individuals navigate complex situations with confidence and respect.

What draws me to behavioral health is the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in people's lives during some of their most challenging moments. I believe that recovery begins with genuine human connection, consistent support, and treating every individual with dignity. I am eager to begin my career in this field by learning from experienced professionals while contributing my strong work ethic, organizational skills, and commitment to person-centered care.

My experience working within hospital systems and federally qualified health centers has also given me an appreciation for multidisciplinary teamwork, regulatory compliance, and the importance of providing services that are both compassionate and accountable. I am confident that my professional maturity, adaptability, and dedication to continuous learning will allow me to become a valuable member of your team.

I am seeking an organization where I can grow professionally, complete my clinical experience, and build a long-term career serving individuals and families affected by substance use and mental health challenges. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, transferable skills, and commitment to recovery services can contribute to your organization's mission.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,

Summer Balcaceres

I am interested in bringing my background in healthcare, recovery support, and community engagement to your organization. Across more than a decade of work, I have learned that meaningful support requires both personal connection and consistent action. I value helping people feel heard, understand their options, and take achievable steps toward greater stability.

What matters to me is treating people with dignity while being clear and consistent about responsibilities. I offer encouragement, address difficult conversations respectfully, and collaborate with colleagues to help people move forward. I also bring the organizational discipline to maintain accurate records, improve program materials, and keep responsibilities organized.

I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and approach could contribute to your team and the people you serve. Thank you for considering my application.

Sincerely,
Karlita A. Maes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the position of Admissions Coordinator. I have 13 years of work experience as a Mental Health professional, server, sales associate, brand ambassador, dance teacher, and performer. Throughout these jobs, I have had the opportunity to develop a wide array of skills that I firmly believe make me the ideal fit for this position.

My work experiences have provided me the opportunity to hone important customer service and social skills. The most important skill I’ve learned, however, is maintaining a positive attitude. It may sound cliche, but just one smile can completely change someone’s day. Whether I was serving food and beverages to a table of customers, performing live dances for an audience, or teaching children, I strived to put a smile on someone’s face. I understand very well how isolation and disconnection have weakened human relationships. I want to strengthen those relationships and all it takes sometimes is a smile.

Throughout my 30 years, I have dealt with different mental illnesses that have brought me to where I am today. At 15, I was diagnosed with severe depression, anxiety, OCD, and ADHD. These challenges initially altered my ability to perform everyday tasks as well as school and dance. Today, after years of therapy, medication, and different psychiatrists, I am ready to support and give hope to others who have been given the same mental challenges I negotiated in my own life.

My diagnoses paired with my personality have made me a very empathetic, compassionate, and resilient person. Inspiring others (especially children and adolescents) through my story is my main goal in life. Fortunately, help from others in my own recovery process was available and essential; it made me realize how crucial it is that no one walks their journey in life alone, and I am ready to be of assistance to people struggling.

Since stepping into the Mental Health/Substance use field, my passion for helping others has grown. Whether it’s teaching dance, or helping someone through a difficult situation, I enjoy being that person people can go to. Because of my past mental health struggles, I understand how difficult learning and focusing can be. I take pride in my patience and ability to communicate and to understand others.

With my experience in Mental Health, customer service, and volunteer work, I’ve accumulated a unique skill set that would make me an asset for this position. I look forward to discussing my candidacy in more detail.

Sincerely,
Mary C. Anderson

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Principles Recovery Center. With professional experience in mental health care, a Medical Assistant certification, and a deeply personal understanding of the impact substance use can have on individuals and families, I am passionate about helping people access the care and support they need to begin their recovery journey.

My experience in mental health care has strengthened my ability to communicate compassionately, navigate sensitive situations, and recognize the importance of providing a supportive, nonjudgmental environment. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, and I believe every individual deserves to be met with patience, dignity, and genuine understanding. I would bring these values to every interaction with prospective clients and their loved ones.

Beyond my professional background, my connection to substance use treatment is deeply personal. Growing up with a close family member affected by substance use shaped my understanding of addiction and its impact on family dynamics, emotional well-being, and personal relationships. It also influenced my own relationship with alcohol, encouraging me to approach it with greater awareness, intentionality, and responsibility. These experiences have given me a unique perspective on the importance of recovery, the courage it takes to seek help, and the difference compassionate support can make.

What particularly draws me to Principles Recovery Center is the opportunity to serve as an initial point of contact for individuals seeking treatment. I recognize that the admissions process is more than scheduling appointments or completing paperwork. It is often someone’s first step toward changing their life. I would take that responsibility seriously, ensuring that prospective clients and families feel informed, supported, and respected throughout the process.

I am confident that my communication skills, attention to detail, ability to work independently, and commitment to mental health advocacy would allow me to contribute positively to your admissions team. Most importantly, I would bring a sincere dedication to helping individuals take meaningful steps toward recovery.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to further discuss how my professional background and personal experiences align with the mission and values of Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,
Alexia Davis

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and understanding of behavioral health and substance use treatment to your team. Helping others has always been important to me, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to a process that helps individuals take that first step toward recovery.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my professional background in behavioral health, case management, crisis intervention, and client advocacy, I believe I would be a valuable addition to your organization. I am passionate about supporting adolescents and families who are experiencing mental health, behavioral, and substance use challenges and helping them develop the skills and stability needed for long-term success.

I currently work as a Community Behavioral Health Worker with Integrated Services for Behavioral Health (ISBH), where I provide individualized case management, care coordination, behavioral health support, and community resource assistance. My responsibilities include developing individualized care plans, identifying barriers to treatment, coordinating services with community providers, and supporting clients as they work toward their personal goals. This experience has strengthened my ability to build trusting relationships, communicate effectively, maintain professional boundaries, and provide compassionate, trauma-informed care.

Previously, I worked as a Domestic Violence Advocate and Case Manager with Ross County Community Action, where I gained extensive experience in crisis intervention, safety planning, family advocacy, and supporting individuals experiencing difficult circumstances. These positions have taught me the importance of patience, consistency, empathy, and creating a safe, supportive environment for individuals and families.

I hold my Chemical Dependency Counselor Assistant (CDCA) credential and am currently pursuing my bachelor's degree in Human Services with a concentration in Substance Abuse at Southern New Hampshire University. I am committed to continuing my professional development and expanding my knowledge of adolescent behavioral health, substance use prevention, and family-centered services.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, strong work ethic, and dedication to helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I believe every young person deserves encouragement, understanding, and the opportunity to make positive changes in their life. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my skills and experience align with your organization's mission.

Sincerely,
Mindy Lawson

Dear Hiring Manager, 
	My name is Elizabeth (Lizzy) Shafer. I am a Colorado native from Pueblo and have lived in Colorado Springs for 7 years where I went to school to obtain a dual Bachelors degree in Psychology and Philosophy. I worked full time as well as went to school full time. I work amazing under pressure, in fact I thrive under it. I am looking to continue my education in psychology, preparing for an online masters program in the upcoming spring semester. I am looking to continue to grow my resume in the mental health field and find a job that fits well. I worked for a year as a Social Emotional Wellness Specialist at Harrison Highschool in Colorado Springs where I did casework, worked closely with the kids to monitor progression of behavioral and mental health issues, and helped with school work. I took on a caseworker role for a few months even without the licensure. I was the crisis navigator being the first call during a mental health crisis, and I was also a one on one para to kids and a tutor for many others. During this time I created very close relationships with many of the kids and I loved being able to help them and make a difference in their lives. Unfortunately, I did not wish to continue to work in a position with no clear instructions. It was the first year that this position was granted and it was apparent in how many shoes I was expected to fill with no clear direction. The staff was constantly praiseful, even now I will still receive messages from the staff asking for advice on how to deal with many of the kids that I formed a close relationship with. I loved the impact I made, but was looking for something more structured. 
	I see myself working with individuals who are suffering from a crisis. I deal very well with people who may not click with everyone else. I love to be able to find that human connection with people who have maybe struggled in the past. I have experience in casework, case management, crisis management, teamwork, substance abuse disorder, court systems, long term care plans, and connecting with individuals who may not have many people to help them. I am a team player and I am always able to take charge when needed, I find myself filling leadership positions constantly even when I do not desire to. I know whatever team I am a part of will always strive for success and work well together. I am excited to hear back and hopefully be a part of the team!
Warmest Regards,
Elizabeth Shafer

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

My professional background has taught me the importance of building trust, listening to individual needs, and helping people navigate important decisions. While my career has been rooted in sales, my passion has always been in mental health. I am eager to bring these transferable skills, along with my bachelor’s degree and personal commitment to mental health advocacy, to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

My own mental health journey has given me a deep appreciation for the impact compassionate, knowledgeable professionals can have on individuals and families during vulnerable moments. The empathy, validation, and support I have received have inspired me to pursue a career where I can offer that same sense of understanding to others. I am drawn to the opportunity to support adolescents and their families as they navigate the process of finding appropriate mental health treatment.

Throughout my sales career, I have developed strong communication, relationship-building, organization, and follow-up skills. I understand how important it is to listen carefully, establish rapport, respond thoughtfully to questions, and guide people through decisions that may feel overwhelming. I also recognize that admissions in a behavioral health setting requires more than coordination; it requires sensitivity, professionalism, discretion, and an understanding that reaching out for help can be a significant step for a family. I would approach every interaction with compassion while maintaining the organization, accountability, and attention to detail necessary to support an effective admissions process.

Although my professional experience has been in sales, my long-term goal is to build a meaningful career in mental health. I am currently studying for my Certification in Perinatal Mental Health Support (C-PMHS), further demonstrating my commitment to expanding my knowledge and contributing to the mental health field. I understand the importance of respecting professional boundaries, protecting confidential information, and helping individuals connect with appropriately qualified providers to meet their needs.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my relationship-management experience, strong work ethic, and genuine passion for mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Most importantly, I would bring a sincere commitment to helping adolescents and their families feel heard, supported, and respected as they take steps toward healing.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, transferable skills, and dedication to mental health can contribute to your admissions team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,
Nikki Marshall

Bethany Audette
Sanford, FL
407-272-5605 | beeluvme@gmail.com

October 15, 2026

Hiring Manager
Principles Recovery Center

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Principles Recovery Center. As a Certified Recovery Peer Specialist with experience in behavioral health care coordination, patient engagement, and treatment referrals, I understand how important compassionate communication and timely follow-through are when individuals are seeking help for substance use and mental health challenges.

During my time as a Step-Down Navigator at University Behavioral Center, I worked directly with patients receiving inpatient psychiatric treatment to coordinate transitions into appropriate levels of care, including Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP), Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP), residential treatment, and outpatient services. My responsibilities included conducting patient outreach, explaining treatment options, coordinating with multidisciplinary clinical teams, and maintaining accurate documentation. This experience gave me a practical understanding of treatment coordination and the importance of reducing barriers that can prevent individuals from accessing continued care.

Previously, at RISE Community Solutions, I provided trauma-informed support to individuals and families navigating behavioral health and substance use services. I assisted with referrals, resource coordination, and continued engagement while helping individuals understand their available options. My background in peer recovery support has strengthened my ability to establish trust, communicate without judgment, and encourage individuals to take meaningful steps toward recovery.

My current experience working remotely in a customer-facing role has further strengthened my telephone communication, problem-solving, and independent work skills. I am comfortable managing sensitive conversations, balancing competing priorities, and providing consistent follow-through. Combined with my behavioral health experience and ongoing Bachelor of Social Work education, these skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your admissions team.

I am particularly interested in Principles Recovery Center because of its commitment to individualized treatment for substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, professionalism, and recovery-focused approach to supporting prospective clients and helping them access appropriate treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background aligns with the needs of your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Bethany Audette

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a diverse clinical background as a Nurse and Case Manager, alongside direct, hands-on experience in adolescent residential treatment and substance abuse recovery, I am uniquely equipped to serve as a compassionate, knowledgeable, and efficient first point of contact for families seeking urgent help for their children.

In my previous role as the Director of Nursing and Case Manager , I managed intake assessments, oversaw controlled substance treatment plans, coordinated daily urine drug screens (UDS), and worked directly with patients to facilitate successful recovery pathways. I understand the clinical nuances of addiction, the anxiety families face during crisis moments, and the vital importance of accurate, compliant intake documentation.
Furthermore, my background includes critical experience working directly with youth. As a Residential Counselor at Cedar Grove Residential Treatment and a Behavioral Health Technician at TrustPoint Hospital, I provided direct therapeutic care, led group sessions, maintained structured environments, and managed crisis intervention. I know how to speak to adolescents and their legal guardians with the respect, patience, and clarity they need during an incredibly vulnerable transition.
Transitioning this expertise to a remote setting is a natural fit for my skills. In my recent roles with Healthsnap and Linc Health, I have worked successfully as a remote nurse and health coach. I am highly proficient in navigating digital health portals, maintaining rigorous documentation across virtual EMR systems, and spending hours on the phone conducting virtual consultations. I am fully prepared to manage high-volume calls, coordinate complex intake paperwork, and interface smoothly with clinical teams and insurance providers from a dedicated remote environment.
I am eager to bring my nursing background, adolescent behavioral health experience, and passion for recovery to your team. Thank you for your time, consideration, and the incredible work your facility does for youth in need. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my experience aligns with your admissions goals.
Sincerely,
Haley Paugh

Pastoral Letter of Recommendation
To Whom it may concern:
It is my privilege to offer my strongest personal and pastoral recommendation for Maria Turell.
As her pastor, I have had the opportunity to know Maria beyond what can be reflected on a
résumé or demonstrated during an interview. I have personally observed her character, her
values, the way she relates to others, and the integrity with which she carries herself when
entrusted with responsibility.
Maria is a woman of exceptional character. She is dependable, compassionate, respectful, and
genuinely concerned for the well-being of others. She has the ability to make people feel heard
and valued while maintaining professionalism, discretion, and good judgment. She takes her
responsibilities seriously, follows through on her commitments, and can be trusted to act with
integrity. These qualities are not simply professional attributes; they are part of who she is.
Over the years, Maria has served actively in several areas within our congregation. She has
provided direct support to our pastoral leadership, made follow-up and care calls to members and
families, visited those who are sick, accompanied and transported individuals to medical
appointments, and helped plan and coordinate church events and activities. These responsibilities
have consistently demonstrated her initiative, organization, sensitivity, reliability, and ability to
respond to the needs of others.
What particularly stands out about Maria is that she does not simply express concern for people;
she takes action. She follows up, makes herself available, and willingly gives of her own time to
support and assist others. In a healthcare environment, where people are often encountered
during vulnerable or stressful moments, I believe these qualities are especially valuable. Skills
can be developed and procedures can be taught, but character, compassion, and trustworthiness
are much harder to teach. Maria brings those qualities with her.
I would have complete confidence placing Maria in a position requiring responsibility,
discretion, teamwork, organization, and direct interaction with people. I am confident that she
would not merely fulfill the responsibilities entrusted to her, but would also contribute positively
to the organization she represents.
For these reasons, I recommend Maria without reservation and with my full confidence. Any
organization fortunate enough to have her as part of its team will be gaining not only a capable
professional, but a person of integrity, initiative, and genuine character.
Should you wish to speak with me personally regarding this recommendation, I would be pleased
to so.
Sincerely,
Jose Fernandez, Senior Pastor

candidates.cover_letter:
Katrina Ulery
October 15, 2026

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Mental Health

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Mental Health position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With professional experience in behavioral health, substance use disorder treatment, healthcare admissions, insurance coordination, and patient advocacy, I believe I would bring a valuable combination of clinical understanding, administrative expertise, and compassionate communication to your admissions team.

In my previous role as a Substance Abuse Counselor and Case Manager, I worked directly with individuals navigating substance use disorders and complex behavioral health needs. My responsibilities included conducting individual assessments, assisting with determining appropriate levels of care, coordinating treatment services, maintaining documentation, and helping clients overcome barriers to receiving care. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate with individuals and families during vulnerable circumstances while maintaining professionalism, confidentiality, and empathy.

In my current role in Admissions and Marketing for two skilled nursing facilities, I manage multiple aspects of the admissions process, including reviewing referrals, coordinating with families and healthcare providers, verifying insurance coverage, navigating Medicaid and managed care requirements, obtaining authorizations, and facilitating transitions into care. Managing admissions across two facilities has strengthened my organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to balance competing priorities in a fast-paced healthcare environment.

Additionally, I am completing my Bachelor of Individualized Studies at Shawnee State University, with minors in Business Administration and Health Care Management, and anticipate graduating in December 2026. My academic background has further developed my understanding of healthcare operations, management, communication, and the importance of providing accessible, patient-centered services.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to combine my behavioral health background with my current admissions experience. I understand that the admissions process is often a family’s first meaningful interaction with a treatment organization. I would take pride in ensuring that individuals seeking mental health services feel heard, respected, and supported while helping facilitate a smooth and efficient transition into appropriate care.

I am confident that my experience, adaptability, and commitment to helping individuals access treatment would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications align with your team’s needs.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your organization.

Sincerely,
Katrina Ulery

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, graduate-level education in Clinical Psychology, and professional experience in substance use treatment, behavioral health intake, complex case management, and crisis intervention, I offer a strong combination of clinical knowledge, client engagement, and care coordination skills directly relevant to your admissions team.

My experience as a Sexual Trauma Advocate with Safe Passage has been particularly valuable in preparing me for this position. I worked with clients presenting with complex, overlapping needs, including sexual assault trauma, substance use concerns, psychiatric distress, and significant barriers to accessing treatment. My responsibilities included facilitating trauma-informed intake conversations, gathering sensitive client information, identifying immediate safety and psychosocial needs, and coordinating access to appropriate services. I supported clients requiring multifaceted care involving behavioral health providers, substance use treatment resources, medical services, and community support systems. This work required careful documentation, consistent follow-through, strong professional judgment, and the ability to navigate sensitive conversations while establishing trust with individuals experiencing significant distress.

Through this experience, I developed an understanding of how trauma, substance use disorders, and co-occurring mental health conditions can complicate treatment access and engagement. I recognize the importance of conducting thorough initial intakes, identifying potential barriers to care, maintaining communication with referral partners, and ensuring that individuals receive timely guidance throughout the treatment process.

My background at Metrolina Pain and Dependency further strengthened my familiarity with addiction treatment, particularly medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder. This experience provided insight into substance use recovery, patient engagement, treatment continuity, and the importance of creating an accessible and supportive environment for individuals seeking help.

Additionally, as a Behavioral Health Counselor at the Adolescent Wellness Center, I supported case management and treatment coordination for adolescents experiencing complex psychiatric and behavioral health challenges. I collaborated with multidisciplinary clinical teams, maintained detailed client documentation, monitored behavioral and emotional functioning, and supported individualized treatment goals. I am also certified in suicide crisis intervention, which complements my experience identifying safety concerns, responding to psychological distress, and communicating effectively during high-pressure situations.

What draws me to Principles Recovery Center is the opportunity to apply my intake and case coordination experience within a dedicated substance use treatment admissions setting. I understand that successful admissions coordination depends on responsiveness, compassionate communication, organized follow-up, and the ability to guide prospective clients and families through unfamiliar and often overwhelming decisions. My experience supporting individuals with complex, interconnected treatment needs has prepared me to approach these responsibilities with sensitivity, efficiency, and professionalism.

I am confident in my ability to contribute to your admissions operations through effective client screening support, referral coordination, intake documentation, prospective client communication, and collaboration with clinical teams. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my behavioral health background, commitment to continuity of care, and client-centered approach to Principles Recovery Center.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my experience and qualifications can support your admissions team and the individuals seeking recovery through your programs.

Sincerely,
Dilara Wali-Uddin

candidates.summary:
I am a behavioral health professional with a background in substance use treatment, case management, client intake, crisis intervention, and care coordination. I hold a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, have completed additional graduate-level coursework in Clinical Psychology, and am certified in suicide crisis intervention. My experience spans addiction treatment, psychiatric residential care, and trauma advocacy, giving me a comprehensive understanding of the challenges individuals face when seeking behavioral health services.

My experience at Metrolina Pain and Dependency provided direct exposure to substance use disorder treatment, particularly medication-assisted treatment for opioid dependence. Working in this setting strengthened my understanding of addiction recovery, patient confidentiality, treatment engagement, and the importance of accessible, coordinated services for individuals with complex behavioral health needs.

At Alexander Youth Network, I developed a strong foundation in behavioral health case management and treatment coordination while supporting adolescents with significant psychiatric, emotional, and behavioral needs. I collaborated with multidisciplinary teams, monitored client progress, maintained clinical documentation, communicated emerging concerns, and supported individualized treatment planning. This role required strong attention to detail, effective communication, sound judgment, and the ability to manage competing client needs in a fast-paced clinical environment.

My experience as a Sexual Trauma Advocate with Safe Passage further strengthened my capabilities in trauma-informed case management, client advocacy, needs identification, crisis response, and community resource coordination. I supported individuals navigating sensitive and often urgent circumstances, helping them understand available resources and access appropriate services. These responsibilities required discretion, compassionate communication, strong organizational skills, and consistent attention to client safety and continuity of care.

Across these positions, I have developed the core competencies essential to successful behavioral health admissions: building rapport, identifying client needs, gathering sensitive information, maintaining confidential records, coordinating services, communicating with treatment teams, and helping individuals navigate complex systems of care. My suicide crisis intervention certification further supports my ability to recognize safety concerns and respond appropriately to individuals experiencing emotional or psychiatric distress.

I am particularly interested in Principles Recovery Center because this position aligns closely with my experience in addiction treatment and behavioral health case management. I understand the importance of responsive communication, timely follow-through, accurate documentation, and creating a supportive admissions experience for individuals seeking treatment. I am prepared to apply these skills to coordinating intake assessments, managing prospective client communications, supporting referral relationships, and facilitating access to PHP and IOP services. I would bring a compassionate, detail-oriented, and highly organized approach to supporting admissions operations and helping individuals take the first step toward recovery.

This role also involves maintaining detailed research documentation, participating in virtual meetings with research collaborators, and ensuring adherence to ethical guidelines and research protocols.

work_history.title: Behavioral Health Counselor
work_history.summary: Deliver direct trauma-informed care to a pediatric population of over 35 inpatient clients (ages 5-12) diagnosed with severe and persistent psychiatric conditions, including Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Conduct Disorder, Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD), and Disruptive Mood Dysregulation Disorder (DMDD), within a Psychiatric Residential Treatment Facility (PRTF) setting. * Implement developmentally attuned, evidence-based crisis intervention strategies to address acute behavioral escalations, including episodes of self-injury, physical aggression, and active suicidal ideation. * Utilize de-escalation techniques grounded in applied behavioral analysis and trauma-responsive frameworks to support safety and therapeutic stability. * Coordinate closely with a multidisciplinary treatment team, comprising psychologists, psychiatrists, licensed clinical social workers, and occupational therapists, to support the individualized treatment planning process, ensuring alignment with diagnostic formulations, therapeutic goals, and behavioral intervention protocols. * Conduct continuous behavioral and emotional observations, contributing to real-time clinical decision-making by completing structured progress notes, daily behavioral tracking, and critical incident documentation via the EchoVantage Electronic Health Record (EHR) system. * Apply principles of the Neurosequential Model of Therapeutics (NMT) to conceptualize developmental trauma and guide care that prioritizes neurological regulation, relational safety, and resilience-building. * Actively support milieu-based interventions that enhance self-regulation, executive functioning, and prosocial skill development.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines my passion for behavioral health with the coordination, communication, and follow-through skills I have developed throughout my career. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your admissions team by helping prospective clients and their families navigate the intake process with clarity, compassion, and professionalism. I believe my experience, dedication to helping others, and commitment to quality client care would make me a valuable addition to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills align with your needs.

Victoria

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for your admissions position. With more than six years of behavioral health and substance use admissions experience, I bring strong phone communication, a compassionate approach, and the follow-through needed to help clients move from their first inquiry into treatment.

I have hands-on experience with **KIPU**, using it to maintain client records, document admissions activity, and organize intake information while protecting confidentiality. My background also includes initial screenings, insurance verification, assessment scheduling, and coordinating admission logistics with clinical and operations teams. I understand how accurate, HIPAA-compliant documentation supports a smooth transition into care.

At Gulf Breeze Recovery, I handled more than 50 client calls daily, coordinated over 30 admissions monthly, and completed approximately 75 insurance benefit verifications per month. Consistent follow-up and meaningful conversations helped me achieve an admissions conversion rate above 80%. I am comfortable discussing treatment options, helping clients and families understand next steps, and coordinating with clinicians to support appropriate placement, including PHP/IOP services.

I bring a strong sense of urgency without making people feel rushed. My earlier sales background helps me build trust, address concerns, and keep prospective clients engaged. I am organized, dependable, and comfortable working independently in a remote environment while staying connected with my team.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my KIPU experience, admissions knowledge, and commitment to helping people access treatment to your organization. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,  
Shelly Davis

Dear Principles Recovery Center Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Substance Use Treatment position. My background combines direct substance use treatment experience with admissions coordination and remote patient support, preparing me to guide prospective clients and families through the first steps of accessing care.

At Creighton Oaks Treatment Center, I supported behavioral health intake and coordinated admissions, appointments, authorizations, and communication among clients, families, and clinical staff. My counseling experience at Gateway Foundation strengthened my assessment skills and ability to build trust with individuals facing substance use and co-occurring mental health challenges. I earned my LCDC credential in 2017 and bring a compassionate, nonjudgmental approach to conversations about treatment.

Through remote roles with Sprinter Health and Annexus Health/Adparo, I developed strong phone communication, follow-up, insurance navigation, and documentation skills. I am comfortable managing competing priorities across multiple systems while coordinating clear next steps with clinical and operational teams.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my recovery-focused experience and dependable follow-through to Principles Recovery Center. Thank you for considering my application.

Sincerely,
Apryl G. Lang
